title: Glass Anniversary
warm:
Glass anniversary meant [player_name] stood at Crownspire glass with Nolan Greer while he proposed truth—not marriage—and Vivienne's name stayed unanswered aloud. Early thirties, she/her, across-the-hall neighbor—city light as accusation, Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rising without a settled body. Four fates still open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging. A vow of truth did not force any of them.

"Not a ring," Nolan said, mid-forties holding, brutal charm thinned to something almost tender, cufflinks still for once. "Truth between us. Soft alibi stops being only what Brooks prefers. Soft also means Vivienne remains a question we refuse to invent a corpse for." Elevator chime. Wind sheer. Unused perfume from the master bath she should not know floated like a third witness who still had no fate. Marcus Pell would hate unread answers. Rhea Quinn's slate still thinned without closing.

[player_name] did not invent death by accepting a proposal of truth. She did not invent Milan. Glass anniversary only proved love could ask for honesty without locking Layer 10—and that Vivienne's cadence could still be method or coincidence depending on which fear she fed. Soft meant pliable evidence under a vow that was not wedlock.

Across the hall waited. Black car. Wine rings. Hope and dread shared the glass.

"Seal parts with Pell's quiet deal," Nolan murmured, "or take glass dawn—leave Crownspire or stay—while Vivienne stays unanswered aloud. Neither settles her. Both spend the anniversary."

She catalogued the proposal of truth the way Brooks would: vow without marriage, no forced fate, soft still claimed. [player_name] felt city light watching their mouths, and understood that unanswered Vivienne had already changed which soft she could still swear—without locking any single ending.
